title: AI vs. AI: Building Resilient Enterprises in the Age of Autonomous Threats

metadata.event: Black Hat Europe 2025 - AI Security Summit

slides.title: AI vs. AI
slides.subtitle: Building Resilient Enterprises in the Age of Autonomous Threats

slides.name: DINIS CRUZ
slides.role:
GenAI Entrepreneur & Former CISO
Akeia.ai / The Cyber Boardroom / MyFeeds.ai
slides.notes: Brief introduction - ex-CISO background, now building AI security tools

slides.title: THE PERFECT STORM
slides.subtitle: Why This Moment Is Different
slides.notes: Transition: Set up the convergence of forces creating unprecedented risk

slides.title: CONVERGING FORCES

children: No liability, loose standards, chronic neglect of NFRs
Tech as second-class concern, inadequate security funding
$Trillions in annual losses by 2025, driven by cybercrime-as-a-service and commoditized attack tools
Creative, persistent, finds alternate paths around restrictions

slides.notes: Key point: These forces were once independent, now they're colliding

slides.title: WE'VE BEEN GETTING AWAY WITH IT
content: AWS: Timing bug wiped out a global database
Azure: Config inconsistency silently propagated, then 'detonated' worldwide
Cloudflare: Routine config change crashed bot defense, halted traffic
CrowdStrike: 8.5 million Windows systems bricked by a faulty update
slides.notes: These weren't sophisticated attacks - they were minor glitches that cascaded. Now imagine if they were deliberate.

slides.title: THE NEW INSIDERS
slides.subtitle: Autonomous Agents as Threat Actors
slides.notes: Transition: Reframe the threat model - it's not just external attackers

slides.title: THREE TYPES OF AI-DRIVEN THREATS

children: Fully autonomous malware that learns and adapts
Your AI bots hijacked via prompt injection
Operating with legitimate access, working for adversary
The paperclip maximizer scenario
Dangerously efficient in ways we didn't anticipate

slides.notes: Prompt injection remains unsolved - any AI taking untrusted input can be subverted

slides.title: HUMAN INSIDERS vs. AI AGENTS

content: Natural limitations on skill/time
Rarely had maximal intent
Fatigue, fear of detection
Single-threaded attacks
Tireless, infinite patience
Machine-speed adaptation
Finds alternate paths when blocked
No moral compass unless constrained

slides.notes: Key insight: We've never had a malicious insider that can instantly devise new approaches when initial attempts fail

slides.title: WHY ENTERPRISES AREN'T READY
slides.subtitle: Fragile by Design
slides.notes: Transition: The uncomfortable truth about our infrastructure

slides.title: BRITTLE ARCHITECTURE

children: ~40% of IT asset value is technical debt (McKinsey)
Systems running 'hot' with minimal safety margins
Internet = circular dependency machine
Identity, DNS, cloud, CDN all rely on each other
Few hard boundaries inside to contain behavior
Not architected for machine-speed internal actors

slides.notes: A failure in one critical service sends ripples across the whole enterprise

slides.title: THE MEASUREMENT PROBLEM
content: Only ~54% have documented disaster recovery plans
Many never test if their backups actually work
Risk registers live in spreadsheets, disconnected from reality
Near-misses treated as one-off glitches, not systemic warnings
No version control for data and configurations
slides.notes: If you don't know exactly what an AI agent did last week, how do you 'undo' it?

slides.title: THE DEFENDER'S EDGE
slides.subtitle: AI as Force Multiplier, Not Black Box
slides.notes: Transition: Here's where we flip the script

slides.title: SECURITY'S ASYMMETRIC ADVANTAGE

children: Access to every system, every data flow
One of few functions focused on business survival
Attackers eventually must do something outside the norm
You define the baseline - they have to deviate from it
Digital twin of the enterprise
Process visibility and provenance at scale

slides.notes: The moment something deviates - an attacker moving laterally OR your own automation spiraling - you catch it

slides.title: AI FOR UNDERSTANDING, NOT BLOCKING

children: Living model of systems, data flows, dependencies
Highlight when anything strays outside known-good pattern
Which agent did what, with which data, when
Convert logs into richly linked, queryable datasets
AI-simulated red team exercises - continuously
Discover attack paths before adversaries do

slides.notes: Don't blindly trust AI to block attacks - use it to illuminate the dark corners

slides.title: RADICAL SIMPLIFICATION
slides.subtitle: The Answer Isn't More Complexity
slides.notes: Transition: Counter-intuitive but essential

slides.title: ASSUME COMPROMISE, CONTAIN BLAST RADIUS

children: Crown-jewel systems walled off with strict controls
One-way isolation for legacy components
Parts may fail, but they fail safely
No cascade into total enterprise failure

content.text: Hardened Boundaries Around What Can't Be Fixed
children: API throttles for fragile older systems
Circuit breakers that halt abnormal transactions

slides.notes: Every AI agent you add to mission-critical systems becomes part of your attack surface

slides.title: FUND NFRs AT UNPRECEDENTED SCALE
content: Comprehensive backup and restore drills - actually test them
Chaos engineering beyond normal peaks
Instrumentation everywhere for real-time visibility
Version control for data, not just code
Consolidate overly complex workflows - fewer moving parts
slides.notes: If it isn't measured or required in contracts, it doesn't get done. Time to change that.

slides.title: DON'T BECOME THE DEPARTMENT OF 'NO'

children: Employees will use AI regardless
Shadow-IT AI is worse than governed AI
Provide vetted platforms and guidelines
Safe internal AI services so they don't run to ChatGPT
Non-engineers creating apps via AI assistance is reality
Establish guardrails and maturity models, don't outlaw it

slides.notes: We did this for cloud - time to do it again for GenAI

slides.title: THE PATH FORWARD
slides.subtitle: From Reactive Firefighting to Proactive Containment
slides.notes: Transition: Wrap up with clear call to action

slides.title: KEY TAKEAWAYS

content.text: AI vs. AI isn't about black-box defenses
children: It's about using AI to finally understand how enterprises actually work

content.text: The race isn't to deploy GenAI defenses faster
children: Every agent becomes part of your attack surface
Assume compromise, model normal, catch deviation

content.text: Security's edge: knowing what 'good' looks like
children: Neither attackers nor runaway agents have anywhere to hide

slides.notes: The winners won't be those who deploy the most AI bots

slides.title: CALL TO ACTION
content: Build your digital twin now - don't wait for a crisis
Invest in visibility, resilience, and continuous learning
Simplify critical paths - remove unnecessary dependencies
Bridge the gap between risk registers and technical reality
Position security as the enabler of safe AI adoption
slides.notes: In this AI vs. AI contest, the side that learns faster and adapts quicker will prevail
